name: Laser Retroreflector Array
description: Eight 1.25-cm corner cube glass retroreflectors embedded in a gold-painted aluminum hemisphere, reflecting laser light back to orbiting spacecraft for precision distance measurements.
scientificQuestion: How accurately can orbital and landing spacecraft determine position relative to surface markers without active power?

name: Neutron Spectrometer System
description: Detects hydrogen-bearing materials by measuring the leakage of thermal and epithermal neutrons from the lunar regolith up to three feet below the surface.
scientificQuestion: What is the abundance and distribution of hydrogenous volatiles and bulk composition in the lunar regolith?

name: Linear Energy Transfer Spectrometer
description: Solid-state silicon Timepix radiation detector measuring the rate of incident ionizing radiation and cosmic rays experienced outside Earth's magnetosphere.
scientificQuestion: What total radiation dose and space weather events will future Artemis astronauts experience on the lunar surface?

name: Near-Infrared Volatiles Spectrometer System
description: Point spectrometer paired with context camera and longwave calibration sensor measuring surface hydration (H2O, OH), CO2, methane, and surface temperatures.
scientificQuestion: What is the mineralogical and volatile composition of lunar regolith at local scale?

name: Peregrine Ion-Trap Mass Spectrometer
leadPi: Barbara Cohen (NASA GSFC) & Simeon Barber (Open Univ.)
description: Ion-trap mass spectrometer characterizing the tenuous lunar exosphere and investigating volatile release from thrusters and surface warming.
scientificQuestion: What volatile species exist in the lunar exosphere and how are they perturbed by lander landings?

name: Lunar Node-1 Navigation Demonstrator
description: CubeSat-class autonomous S-band radio navigation beacon using Multi-spacecraft Autonomous Positioning System (MAPS) algorithms to provide GPS-like positioning.
scientificQuestion: Can a decentralized network of surface beacons provide reliable autonomous navigation for landing, orbital, and surface assets?

name: Stereo Cameras for Lunar Plume-Surface Studies
description: Suite of four miniature stereo cameras capturing 3D photogrammetry of the engine exhaust plume scouring and cratering the regolith during final descent.
scientificQuestion: How much erosion and particle blast is produced by rocket plumes impacting the lunar surface at touchdown?

name: Radio-wave Observations of the photo-Electron Sheath
description: Low-frequency radio spectrometer (10 kHz - 30 MHz) with storable monopole antennas measuring the photoelectron sheath density 1-2 meters above the surface.
scientificQuestion: What is the density and scale height of the Moon's photoelectron sheath, and what solar/Jupiter radio bursts can be detected?

name: Navigation Doppler Lidar
description: Triple-beam coherent laser Doppler radar measuring altitude and 3-axis velocity vectors with millimeter-level precision. Famously patched in real-time to guide IM-1's descent.
scientificQuestion: Can laser Doppler ranging replace heavy radar systems to ensure tight landing dispersions and soft touchdowns on hazardous planetary surfaces?

name: Radio Frequency Mass Gauge
description: Uses RF electromagnetic resonance modes inside cryogenic propellant tanks to measure liquid methane and oxygen quantity in low/micro-gravity environments.
scientificQuestion: How accurately can cryogenic propellant mass be measured in zero-g without settled liquid levels?

name: Laser Retroreflector Array (IM-1)
description: Permanent passive optical reflector mounted to Nova-C deck, serving as an enduring location marker on Malapert A crater rim.
scientificQuestion: Can passive laser markers provide long-term geodetic reference points for future lunar orbiters and landers?

name: Next Generation Lunar Retroreflector
description: Large single 100-mm corner cube retroreflector enabling sub-millimeter Earth-to-Moon laser ranging accuracy, improving on Apollo-era precision by 10x.
scientificQuestion: What can sub-millimeter Earth-Moon ranging reveal about lunar interior core fluid motion and General Relativity?

name: Radiation Tolerant Computer System
description: FPGA computing system implementing real-time fault mitigation architectures with three sensitivity-tuned radiation dosimeters to withstand ionizing radiation.
scientificQuestion: Can commercial FPGA architecture achieve radiation fault tolerance without expensive custom rad-hard silicon?

name: Regolith Adherence Characterization
description: Exposes 30 material samples on rotating wheels to determine regolith adhesion rates, dust shedding effectiveness, and optical/thermal degradation.
scientificQuestion: Which materials best resist abrasive lunar regolith adhesion on spacesuits, solar arrays, and optical sensors?

name: Lunar Magnetotelluric Sounder
description: Electrometer and fluxgate magnetometer measuring natural electric and magnetic field variations to determine mantle electrical conductivity down to 1,000 km depth.
scientificQuestion: What is the thermal profile, hydration state, and composition of the Moon's deep mantle beneath Mare Crisium?

name: Lunar Environment Heliospheric X-ray Imager
description: Wide field-of-view soft X-ray imager (0.1–2 keV) viewing Earth from the Moon to capture solar wind charge exchange with Earth’s dayside magnetopause.
scientificQuestion: How does solar wind energy couple into Earth's magnetosphere to trigger geomagnetic storms and space weather disturbances?

name: Lunar PlanetVac
description: Pneumatic surface sampling system mounted on a lander footpad using pressurized gas pulses to blast regolith into a transfer tube and collection sieve.
scientificQuestion: Can low-mass pneumatic gas injection reliably collect surface regolith without complex mechanical robotic arms?

name: Subsurface Thermal Exploration with Rapidity
description: Pneumatically drilled probe penetrating 2 to 3 meters into regolith to measure thermal gradient and thermal conductivity, determining planetary heat flow.
scientificQuestion: What is the primordial heat flow emanating from the lunar interior through an unperturbed basaltic basin?

name: Stereo Cameras for Plume-Surface Studies (v1.1)
description: Enhanced 6-camera stereo imaging system triggering at higher altitudes to provide comprehensive before-and-after photogrammetry of landing pad cratering.
scientificQuestion: How accurately can transient multi-camera photogrammetry validate computational fluid dynamics models of plume-regolith erosion?

name: Electrodynamic Dust Shield
description: Dynamic electrostatic cleaning electrode system embedded in transparent glass and thermal radiator panels, lifting and repelling dust particles without moving parts.
scientificQuestion: Can electrodynamic traveling waves reliably clear abrasive lunar dust from cameras and thermal radiators under real lunar surface gravity and vacuum?

name: Lunar GNSS Receiver Experiment
leadPi: Fabio Dovis (Politecnico di Torino) & Joel Parker (NASA GSFC)
description: High-sensitivity dual-frequency receiver tracking faint Earth-based GPS and Galileo constellation sidelobe signals at lunar distances for autonomous positioning.
scientificQuestion: Can existing Earth GNSS constellations provide operational navigation and timing solutions for cislunar spacecraft and surface missions?

name: The Regolith and Ice Drill for Exploring New Terrains
description: 1-meter rotary percussive drill capable of penetrating cryogenic regolith and rock at -180°C, bringing samples to the surface in 10-cm bites.
scientificQuestion: What is the mechanical strength, depth, and temperature profile of subsurface icy regolith at the lunar South Pole?

name: Mass Spectrometer Observing Lunar Operations
description: Modified quadrupole mass spectrometer analyzing sublimating volatile molecules (H2O, CO2, CO, CH4, NH3) from drill cuttings on the surface.
scientificQuestion: What is the concentration, isotopic signature, and volatile composition of subsurface polar ice deposits?

name: Lunar Vertex PRISM-1 Suite
leadCenter: Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory
description: Lander and rover magnetometer suite paired with multispectral microscope and plasma spectrometer to explore Reiner Gamma swirl in situ.
scientificQuestion: How does the crustal magnetic anomaly interact with solar wind to produce high-albedo lunar swirls?

name: Cooperative Autonomous Distributed Robotic Exploration
description: Trio of shoe-box sized autonomous rovers acting as a collaborative multi-agent swarm with multistatic ground-penetrating radar to create 3D subsurface maps.
scientificQuestion: Can decentralized autonomous robotic swarms coordinate without human direction to map hazardous planetary terrain?

name: FARSIDE Seismic Suite
description: Two ultra-sensitive seismometers (VBB and SP) housed inside an autonomous vacuum-insulated vault designed to survive the 14-day freezing lunar night in Schrödinger Basin.
scientificQuestion: What is the seismic activity and mantle structure of the lunar far side, and does it differ from the Apollo nearside measurements?

name: Lunar Surface Electromagnetics Experiment - Night
leadCenter: NASA / U.S. Dept of Energy (Brookhaven / LBNL)
description: Low-frequency radio astronomy observatory with 3-meter monopole antennas operating during lunar night on the far side to measure the cosmological Dark Ages 21-cm hydrogen line.
scientificQuestion: What were the cosmological conditions and dark matter interactions during the universe's Dark Ages before the ignition of the first stars?

name: Lunar Vulkan Imaging and Measurement Suite
description: Suite of visible, near-infrared, and gamma-ray/neutron spectrometers mounted on a rover and lander to explore the silicic volcanic Gruithuisen Domes.
scientificQuestion: How did silicic volcanism evolve on a dry, unsegmented planet lacking plate tectonics and abundant water?
